pageCache.pageTitle: Arnold House School | Private Prep School for Boys London
pageCache.text:
Founded in 1905, Arnold House is a central London school with exceptional facilities. A thriving school, fully committed to outstanding pastoral care allowing each boy to reach his full potential both in the classroom and beyond.
Every Boy, Seen & Celebrated
Arnold House is a leading independent London preparatory school for boys aged 3 to 13. Located in the heart of St John’s Wood, we combine tradition and academic rigour with a modern, boy-centred approach to education. Our boys go on to top senior schools — but more importantly, they leave with strong values, confidence, and a clear sense of who they are.
We are proud to offer a 10-year journey that nurtures each boy academically, socially and emotionally — from his very first day in Reception to senior school preparation at 11+ and 13+. Every step is shaped by our commitment to whole-child development, exceptional pastoral care, and a strong sense of community.
Arnold House Joins The St Paul's School Group
Arnold House is delighted to announce that it will join The St Paul’s School Group from November 2026.
As part of the Group, Arnold House boys will benefit from the St Paul’s Programme, a holistic enrichment offering spanning academic and life skills, leadership, wellbeing initiatives and Group-wide competitions. The St Paul’s School Stewarded Pathway will also provide a supported route to St Paul’s School for boys within the Group, including early identification and enrichment support, the potential for pre-Year 6 offers, and direct access to St Paul’s academic staff for targeted development in areas like maths and English.
Pre-Prep
Pre-Prep includes Early Years, Pre-Reception and Reception, and Year 1. At this vital stage, we set solid foundations for future learning — nurturing curiosity, confidence and a love of discovery.
Prep
Prep includes Years 2–8 and builds on early learning with stretch, challenge and opportunities to lead. Boys gain the knowledge, habits and character to succeed at senior school and in life.
Grounded. Well-Rounded. Future-Ready.
A Purposeful All-Boys Education
We are all-boys by choice — not just by tradition. Every decision is made through the lens of how boys learn, grow and flourish best. Our specialist team, outstanding facilities and tailored teaching methods help each pupil thrive as a learner and as a person.
Learning with Space to Breathe
Our boys enjoy weekly time at our Canons Park site — a rare offering for a London prep school — giving them the chance to explore, create, and thrive in the outdoors. These days build confidence, wellbeing and joy, complementing the pace of city life with fresh air and freedom.
Academic Excellence, Tailored Support
From Early Years to 13+, we help boys reach their potential — with a strong track record of success at top senior schools and a focus on learning habits that last a lifetime.
Whole-Boy Development
We see boys as individuals — sons, brothers, friends and citizens — not just pupils. Our values-led approach supports every aspect of their growth, building character, empathy and self-belief
Discover Exceptional Facilities For Boys To Thrive
Our purpose-built Canons Park facility offers a rare and exceptional extension to city-based learning: weekly days for outdoor learning, sports, the arts and creative exploration in natural surroundings. It’s one of the many ways we help boys thrive with space to breathe — developing confidence, resilience and joy beyond the classroom.
His Journey Starts Here
Arnold House boys are known for being confident, kind, curious and grounded. They are supported every step of the way — not just to succeed, but to flourish.
Come and see how your son could thrive at Arnold House.
Arnold House Boys Continue Their Educational Journey at Top Senior Schools in London and Beyond

pageCache.pageTitle: Values | Arnold House School | Independent Boys School London
pageCache.text:
We are a dynamic, values-driven community, offering an enriching and seamless educational journey designed to inspire and support boys from the age of 3 through to 13.
A Ten Year Journey
This ten-year journey offers a stable & supportive environment where boys can develop physically, emotionally and socially through the key stages of their growth and progression. In turn they will gain experience, learn skills and embed knowledge in a wide variety of disciplines: an exceptional team of dedicated staff inspiring excellence in every area supported by outstanding facilities and resources.
We are all-boys by choice, not simply by tradition: this approach extends a boy’s positive experience of school to all parts of the curriculum, maximising his potential.
Our pedagogy embraces dynamic, hands-on teaching methods that cultivate academic excellence, personal growth, and leadership.
This empowers boys to become confident, well-rounded individuals who are intellectually curious, independent/critical thinkers, with authentic personalities and the ability to be comfortable with difference and socially adapt.
We continually assess our methods through an all-boys lens to ensure that we are best meeting their needs; this allows us to tailor the boys’ social development and emotional wellbeing alongside their educational growth.
At all stages, we are welcoming young boys into our care, who have unique personalities, innate curiosity and minds full of ideas. We see them as boys, brothers and sons, not simply pupils. We celebrate individuality and self-expression at school.
We value the importance of a collaborative approach working with parents
In a world that is constantly evolving, we cannot predict the future career landscape, but we know that a positive mindset, and a range of prosocial qualities will always be valued.
In this long-term view, our measure of academic growth is not just in the grades or certificates continuously achieved here, but in the boys’ active engagement in what they do, whatever their level of mastery. Each boy has the same opportunity to reach their potential – in the classroom, on the sports field or on stage – and we expect them to be active and fully engaged in all areas of school life.
By committing to our longer timescale, parents will better see their son’s growing strengths and passions, helping inform the decision on where he should continue his education. We do not prepare for 7+, 8+ or 10+ transfers, but provide outstanding, bespoke support for 11+ and 13+ applications.
We are mindful that all our boys will eventually transfer to another school. Our aim is, therefore, to develop outstanding individuals who will contribute positively to their communities, embrace new opportunities and possess excellent learning skills. With the ability to excel in any chosen field, they will be well prepared to thrive at top schools beyond Arnold House.
Industry and Citizenship
Industry encapsulates intrapersonal skills, such as ambition, attention to detail, practice, preparation, determination and a growth mindset.
Citizenship promotes qualities of teamwork, collaboration, public performance, care, helpfulness and emotional intelligence.
Both Industry and Citizenship are extended into all areas and year groups of the school by our emphasis on the ‘Three Rs’: at all times we teach boys to be Ready, Respectful and Responsible.

pageCache.pageTitle: About | Arnold House School | Private Boy's School in London
pageCache.text:
A Message From The Headmaster
A Vision for Education. Our school, and my personal vision of education, was built on one simple belief: There are no limits on what a well-rounded and well-grounded boy can achieve.
‘Education’ at Arnold House is not simply about ticking boxes; it’s about creating a wider foundation for growth and development, igniting a passion for learning, feeding curiosity and fulfilling every facet of personal potential.
As well as excelling in the classroom, Arnold House boys will succeed in the concert hall, the art studio, on the playing field and in the wider world, too. And because we place equal emphasis on social and spiritual development, our boys learn invaluable lessons about living with others, the value of a code of conduct and the joys of sharing activities with others.
Whilst the curriculum is designed to help every boy reach and thrive at his senior school, I firmly believe that a first-class education will always go further in truly preparing our boys for life beyond the classroom and for the challenges of tomorrow.
The results speak for themselves.
Today, our school has an enviable reputation for developing bright, considerate, and ambitious boys who continue to succeed far beyond Arnold House.
The following pages offer more insight into the ethos and culture of Arnold House, and we look forward to welcoming you.
Explore More
Ethos & Aims
History
Admissions

At Arnold House, we are proud to offer our boys a rich array of experiences through well-established and meaningful partnerships. These collaborations enhance their personal, academic, and social development, while fostering a strong sense of community engagement.
Community Service
Community service is central to life at Arnold House. Throughout the year, our boys take part in numerous charitable initiatives, working with both local and national organisations.
We have proudly partnered with St John’s Hospice for over 30 years, supporting their vital work within the local hospital. Our pupils also regularly contribute to food banks, homelessness outreach projects, an annual beach clean (Surfers Against Sewage), community litter picking (Canons Park) and other and other national charities, developing empathy and a sense of responsibility along the way.
Girls’ School
Arnold House maintains strong ties with nearby girls’ schools, including Queen’s College Prep and Sarum Hall. These partnerships offer valuable opportunities for boys and girls to learn and collaborate together in a school setting.
Recent joint initiatives have included workshops at Canons Park and a collaborative concert at the local chapel, fostering mutual respect, teamwork, and friendship.
Tooled Up Education
We are proud to be a Tooled Up Education School, providing our families and staff with access to an extensive digital library of evidence-based resources on parenting, education, and wellbeing.
Founded by Dr Kathy Weston, Tooled Up Education offers expert advice on topics such as children’s mental health, digital wellbeing, academic success, and family relationships. Parents can attend regular expert-led talks and access practical tools to help support their child’s development both at school and at home.
Oppidan Education
Arnold House is pleased to continue our dynamic partnership with Oppidan Education, a mentoring organisation dedicated to nurturing confidence, communication skills, and character in young people.
Our Year 5 and 6 boys take part in one-to-one mentoring and group workshops designed to promote oracy, self-awareness, and resilience. These sessions provide a supportive space for personal growth, whether preparing for interviews, navigating social dynamics, or discovering individual strengths.
Let’s Leap
In partnership with Let’s Leap, Arnold House offers a high-quality Extended Day programme, giving families the flexibility they need while ensuring children remain safe, stimulated, and engaged after school.
As an Ofsted-registered provider, Let’s Leap offers a broad range of creative and recreational activities, delivered by specialists who understand the importance of play, learning, and wellbeing beyond the classroom.

pageCache.pageTitle: Supporting Emotional Wellbeing in Children by Helping Small Worries Before They Grow | Arnold House School
pageCache.text:
All children experience worries at some stage of childhood, whether it is separating from a parent in Pre Reception, navigating friendships or managing expectations as they grow older. Supporting emotional wellbeing in children means helping them recognise, express and manage these worries early, before small concerns begin to affect learning, relationships and confidence.
At Arnold House, we support boys from the age of three through to Year 8, and understand that children’s worries naturally change alongside their emotional, social and cognitive development. Rather than removing worry altogether, our role as adults, both at home and at school, is to provide the reassurance, guidance and emotional support children need to build resilience over time.
How Childhood Worries Change with Age
As children grow, the nature of their worries changes alongside their emotional, social and cognitive development. Understanding these different stages helps adults provide the reassurance and support children need at each age.
Common Worries in the Pre Prep Years
In the Pre‑Prep years, common worries often include separation from parents, unfamiliar adults, toileting, loud noises, changes to routine, or fear of “getting something wrong.” At this age, worries are rarely expressed through words. Instead, they may show up as tears, clinginess, physical complaints or withdrawal. These responses are developmentally typical and signal a need for reassurance and calm, consistent adult support. This is why the Key Person role in Pre‑Reception is so important. Having a trusted adult who knows each boy well helps children feel safe, understood and secure as they transition from home to school.
From around Year 2, boys become more self‑aware and begin to compare themselves with others. Worries may focus on friendships, fairness, rules, making mistakes or seeking adult approval. As emotional regulation skills are still developing, these worries can sometimes escalate quickly if a child feels uncertain or under pressure.
Understanding Anxiety in Older Children
As boys move into the older years, academic demands, peer relationships and concerns about “fitting in” may become more prominent. At this stage, boys are often less likely to talk openly about worry. Instead, anxiety may be expressed through humour, avoidance or frustration—behaviours that can appear challenging but often signal underlying uncertainty.
Supporting Emotional Wellbeing for Children in School
In Pre‑Reception and Reception, Personal, Social and Emotional Development (PSED) sits at the heart of the curriculum. Boys are supported to build secure relationships with trusted adults, recognise and name their feelings, manage emotions and behaviour, and develop confidence and independence.
The Importance of Emotional Safety in Learning
Research shows that when children feel emotionally safe and securely connected, they are far more able to learn and regulate their emotions. When stress or anxiety is high, the brain prioritises survival over learning, making concentration and problem‑solving much harder.
As boys progress through the school, these principles are embedded rather than replaced. PSED evolves into PSHE, supported by predictable routines, clear boundaries, opportunities for reflection and a culture that values effort, kindness and self‑regulation.
These opportunities to build confidence, independence and emotional resilience extend beyond the classroom through everyday school experiences, including outdoor play, collaborative learning and the wider pastoral environment across the school.
Learn more about The Importance of Outdoor Play in Early Years Education
Discover more about Outdoor Learning Opportunities at Canons Park
Building Emotional Regulation and Resilience
Children cannot learn to self‑regulate until they have first been co‑regulated by calm, consistent adults. When adults notice small changes early, help children name their feelings, and reassure them that “it’s okay to feel like this,” worries are far less likely to become overwhelming. Guiding children towards manageable strategies, rather than immediately fixing the problem, builds confidence and resilience over time.
Working Together to Support Emotional Wellbeing
When school and home share a common language around emotions, coping and reassurance, children thrive. Talking openly about feelings, modelling calm responses to stress and giving boys time and space to practise emotional regulation all help them develop lifelong skills.
Preparing Children for Lifelong Emotional Wellbeing
Supporting emotional development from the earliest years in Pre Prep and throughout Prep School equips our boys with far more than academic knowledge. It lays the foundations for self-awareness, empathy, resilience and confidence – skills they will carry well beyond the classroom. Helping children manage small worries early is not only preventative; it is one of the most important investments we can make in their future wellbeing.
At Arnold House, we believe that emotional wellbeing and learning go hand in hand. By creating an environment where boys feel safe, understood and supported at every stage of their development, we help them build the confidence and resilience needed to thrive both in school and beyond.
Victoria McKenzie Head of Pre-Prep

pageCache.pageTitle: The History of Arnold House School | Boys Prep School London
pageCache.text:
A Tradition Founded In St John's Wood
Established in 1905 by Miss Amy Hanson, Arnold House started its first term with just nine pupils. During these early days, Miss Hanson would borrow a carriage from a well-known St John’s Wood doctor, so that she could be seen driving around the neighbourhood in order to bring herself to the notice of prospective parents. Just after the turn of the century, Miss Hanson’s real task was to demonstrate that a headmistress could prepare boys for Public School as well as any headmaster. She did compete successfully with her male counterparts and the school flourished.
In 1937, Miss Hanson was joined by Mr George Smart who succeeded her as Head two years later. Mr Smart was Headmaster for thirty years, retiring in 1969, having been instrumental in making the school an educational charitable trust in that same year. Of this accomplishment Mr Smart said, “This was in line with the policy of many other preparatory schools which thus escaped the charge of being run for profit. Much more importantly it meant that schools were no longer dependent on the policies of one man alone and provided a surer guarantee of continuity to parents.”
Mr John Pepys (1969-1977) and Mr Jonathan Clegg (1977-1994) oversaw the general expansion of the school and were responsible for continuing the traditions established by their predecessors, with an emphasis on the values of courtesy, respect for the individual and consideration for others.
Mr Nicholas Allen took over from Jonathan Clegg in 1994 and moved on to Newton Prep School, Battersea, in 2006. During Nicholas Allen’s time as Headmaster the school underwent many changes. Pupil numbers increased overall and, to accommodate this expansion, the school undertook a major building and refurbishment programme. Balance and breadth were the school’s watchwords over the last decade or so and, as a result, the school thrived in all spheres.
Mr Vivian Thomas took over as Headmaster in September 2006 to further develop the School’s achievements on the basis that ‘Happy boys will learn.’ He had previously worked at Arnold House as Head of Mathematics and Deputy Head, leaving in 2001 to take the Headship of Keble School in Winchmore Hill. Upon his retirement in 2021, Giles Tollit became the sixth Head of Arnold House, having completed ten years as Head of Horris Hill a leading boys’ boarding prep school in Newbury, Berkshire. Giles joined Arnold House at a time of change, seeing through the addition of the Pre-Prep site in Marlborough Place and integration of two new year groups (Pre-Reception and Reception) whilst continuing to develop the School’s reputation for outstanding pastoral care and academic excellence.

Independent Schools Council
The Independent Schools Council brings together seven associations of independent schools, their heads, bursars and governors.
Through their member associations they represent over 1,200 independent schools in the UK and overseas. These schools are ranked among the best in the world and educate more than half a million children each year.
The Independent Association of Prep Schools
The Independent Association of Prep Schools (IAPS) is a schools association with around 650 of the world’s leading prep schools in membership.
Schools must reach a very high standard to be eligible for membership, with strict criteria on teaching a broad curriculum, maintaining excellent standards of pastoral care and keeping staff members’ professional development training up to date.

pageCache.pageTitle: Independent School Jobs in London | Arnold House School
pageCache.text:
If you’re passionate about education in the broadest sense and making a real difference to the pupils you teach, Arnold House could be a great place for you to progress your career.
Whether you are starting out or seeking new challenges, we will invest in you and support you on your professional journey.
About Arnold House
Arnold House is a top London boys’ prep school, with two form entry (20 boys in a class) from Pre-Reception to Year 8. We are an independent school and a charitable trust, overseen by our experienced Governing Board.
As a thriving prep school, we value an all-round education as key to boys’ success as they progress on to their senior schools. Academically boys excel, but they also have opportunities to thrive on the sports field, in music, drama and art, as well as many chances to go on school trips and visits, which create life-long memories.
Why Arnold House?
Here’s why Arnold House could be the perfect environment for your next step:
Small class sizes allow for truly personalised attention. Get to know each boy as an individual, nurturing their unique talents and supporting their development at every turn.
At Arnold House we have the flexibility to design dynamic and engaging lessons, encouraging creativity, independent thought, and a genuine love of learning. Your ideas and passion will help shape the curriculum design.
At Arnold House we are dedicated to fostering well-rounded individuals. You’ll play a vital role in developing essential life skills, strong values, and a robust pastoral care system that supports every child’s emotional and social wellbeing.
Benefit from well-resourced environments, state-of-the-art facilities for sports, arts, music, and digital learning. These resources provide exciting opportunities to enrich your teaching and offer a wide array of co-curricular activities.
Become part of a close-knit, collaborative community where colleagues, parents, and leadership are all invested in pupil success. Access generous professional development opportunities and a culture that values and rewards your contributions.
Experience working with highly motivated boys and involved parents who are deeply committed to their children’s education. This shared dedication creates a positive and supportive learning atmosphere for everyone.
While academic rigour is paramount, the curriculum at Arnold House allows you freedom from too much high-stakes standardised testing, allowing you to focus on genuine understanding, critical thinking, and a deeper exploration of subjects.
Whether you are a teacher or member of the wider support team, the working environment is supportive and inspiring. Staff wellbeing is key to our approach, with great professional development opportunities, generous non-contact periods, regular social events, and a reflective approach to ensuring everyone has the support they need to focus on their role.
Staff work incredibly hard, but the friendships and bonds you build with colleagues highlight the school’s real strength.
I love working at Arnold House because of its strong family atmosphere. Staff genuinely enjoy working with one another and with the boys.
We are all deeply committed to the boys, our colleagues, and the school’s success—something you can see in the care and passion behind our everyday actions.
“Arnold House offers excellent professional development opportunities, and I believe staff are generously recognised and rewarded for their efforts.
Arnold House quickly becomes like a second family. From day one, you feel truly welcome.
Small Class Sizes, Big Impact
Holistic Education & Character Development
Exceptional Resources & Facilities
Supportive Community & Professional Growth
Engaged Pupils & Parents
Focus on Excellence, Not Just Tests
Close Knit and Supportive Professional Environment
Safeguarding At Arnold House
Arnold House is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and applicants must be willing to undergo child protection screening appropriate to the post, including checks with past employers and the Disclosure and Barring Service.
Current Vacancies
Arnold House was founded in 1905 in St John’s Wood. It is an independent preparatory school located in London, NW8, for boys from 3 to 13, and a member of IAPS (Independent Association of Prep Schools). In November we will become part of the St Paul’s Group, a family of leading preparatory schools brought together by a shared commitment to educational excellence. In our recent ISI inspection it was reported that pupils’ academic achievement and personal development are both excellent.
We are seeking an enthusiastic, versatile and inspiring Assistant Director of Music to join our Music Department and contribute to the vibrant musical life of the school.
The successful candidate will be an accomplished musician and passionate teacher who is able to inspire pupils from Pre-Reception to Year 8. They will work closely with the Director of Music and colleagues across the school to deliver an engaging and ambitious Music curriculum, whilst also contributing to performances, assemblies, productions and the wider co-curricular life of the school.
The role would particularly suit a musician who is a confident pianist and accompanist with the flexibility and enthusiasm to work across a wide range of musical activities.
In addition you will support the Director of Music with much of the involved work of running a busy and complex department, for instance helping with the organisation of concerts, timetabling of individual music lessons with our peripatetic music teachers, liaise with parents about the availability of instrumental sessions and help with the organisation of ABRSM music exams.
We offer a competitive salary and pension, a friendly work environment, free lunches during term time.
In January we were awarded School Mental Health Gold Award by the Carnegie Centre of Excellence for Mental Health in Schools. Our school is known for its family ethos and being a great place to work. We are committed to promoting and protecting the mental and physical health of all our staff.
Application Pack Recruitment Policy Privacy Notice Application Form
Read the Application Pack, our Recruitment and Selection policy, download an application form and send a covering letter to recruitment@arnoldhouse.co.uk explaining why you are suitable for the role. In the case of any queries, please contact Frances Peel Yates, HR Manager on fpeelyates@arnoldhouse.co.uk.
Deadline for applications is 9am on Monday 12th October. Start date: January 2027
Arnold House School is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and young people and expects all staff to share in this commitment. Applicants will be required to undergo child protection screening appropriate to the post, including checks with past employers and the Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS). The post is exempt from the Rehabilitation of Offenders Act 1974 and the school is permitted to ask applicants to declare all cautions and convictions.

pageCache.pageTitle: The Arnold House Parents' Association (AHPA) | Arnold House School
pageCache.text:
We believe a strong, connected community is at the heart of a truly exceptional education. The Arnold House Parents’ Association (AHPA) plays a vital role in fostering this sense of belonging, creating opportunities for boys, parents, and staff to come together and celebrate school life beyond the classroom.
Events Throughout The Year
The AHPA organises three major events each year—one every term—that are highlights of the school calendar: Fireworks Night in the Autumn Term, Quiz Night in the Spring Term, and the activity-packed Family Summer Fair. Alongside these flagship events, the AHPA hosts a range of fun initiatives throughout the year, from exciting competitions to ice-pop and tuckshop sales for the boys.
This dynamic parent-led organisation is funded through the generous support of the entire Arnold House parent community, helping to ensure these memorable experiences are open to every family.
Join The AHPA
Parents who join the AHPA team not only contribute meaningfully to school life but also forge lasting friendships within our warm and welcoming community. Opportunities exist both for those who wish to be part of the core planning group, from across each section of the school, who help bring events to life.
At Arnold House, we’re proud of the unique partnership between parents and the school—one that enriches every boy’s journey. If you are a parent or future parent and would like to find out how to get involved, please contact the team at ahpa@arnoldhouse.co.uk or click on the button below.

Assigned during the staggered start process, a boy’s key person—usually the class teacher or a teaching assistant—acts as a dedicated guide throughout the year. Key information and observations are shared with parents via Tapestry, our online learning journal. Biannual meetings between the Head of Pre-Prep and class teachers take place in the Autumn and Summer Terms to review each child’s progress and wellbeing.

pageCache.pageTitle: Pastoral Care at Arnold House Prep School | Arnold House School
pageCache.text:
At Arnold House, the wellbeing of every boy is at the heart of all that we do. We believe individual care and attention is essential for every child to feel safe, valued, and engaged—our pastoral provision is second to none.
A Supportive And Caring Environment
From the moment a boy joins Arnold House, he becomes part of a warm and nurturing school community. Form Teachers offer daily support and are always available to guide, encourage, and listen. Heads of Year provide an additional layer of care, monitoring both pastoral and academic development closely.
Our full-time School Nurse works in close collaboration with staff and the catering team to oversee all medical and dietary needs, ensuring every boy is cared for in a holistic way. The entire staff team plays an active role in promoting mental health and wellbeing, working closely with families to support each child as an individual.
Learning About Wellbeing
Through form time, assemblies, and our PSHE (Personal, Social, Health, and Economic) curriculum, boys learn to understand and care for their own mental and physical wellbeing. Special events, such as Children’s Mental Health Week and Wellbeing Week, offer opportunities for reflection, discussion, and community connection.
We are proud to partner with Tooled Up Education, giving Arnold House families free access to a library of evidence-based resources, expert advice, and webinars designed to support children’s emotional development at home and in school.
Voice, Values And Belonging
Every boy at Arnold House is encouraged to have a voice. We strive to ensure that every child feels included, accepted, and understood. Whether excelling academically, on the sports field, or through quiet everyday kindness, all boys are recognised and celebrated for their unique contributions.
Our House System plays a central role in fostering community and character. Each boy belongs to one of four Houses, promoting friendship across year groups and encouraging values such as Industry and Citizenship. House Points are awarded for positive behaviour, academic effort, and teamwork, contributing to a shared sense of achievement and pride.
Recognising Achievement And Encouraging Growth
Each week, our Citizenship Assembly is a highlight of school life—a chance to recognise hard work, kindness, and character. House Points earned throughout the week are celebrated, and achievements in sport, music, drama, and beyond are awarded with certificates, badges, or ties.
Our reward system focuses on positivity and encouragement, with recognition significantly outweighing sanctions. Boys may earn:
While our focus is on reinforcement and growth, clear behavioural expectations are maintained. When needed, conduct penalties provide a framework for reflection and improvement. These are handled sensitively, with support from Heads of Year and communication with parents where appropriate.
Industry badges or ties for consistent effort
Working In Partnership With Families
We believe pastoral care is most effective when school and homework in close partnership. If your son is facing challenges—whether personal, academic, or social—we encourage you to reach out. Our staff are here to listen, support, and work collaboratively with you to ensure every boy thrives.

pageCache.pageTitle: Safeguarding | Arnold House School | Boys Prep School London
pageCache.text:
At Arnold House, we are fully committed to ensuring the safety, wellbeing, and protection of every pupil in our care.
Our Commitment
Our aim is to create a nurturing, supportive environment where all children feel safe, respected, and able to thrive.
Arnold House provides a secure and inclusive community in which pupils can learn and grow with confidence. We believe every child has the right to feel protected, heard, and supported – and we work tirelessly to uphold those rights.
We expect all members of our school community – including staff, governors, parents, and visitors – to share in our commitment to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children.
Policies & Practice
Our safeguarding policies are aligned with statutory guidance, including Keeping Children Safe in Education (KCSIE), and are regularly reviewed to reflect best practice. All staff and volunteers receive appropriate training and are familiar with the procedures for reporting concerns.
We are vigilant in areas such as:
Child protection and welfare
Online and digital safety
Mental health and emotional wellbeing
Prevent duty and radicalisation
Designated Safeguarding Leads
Arnold House has a strong safeguarding team in place, led by trained Designated Safeguarding Leads (DSLs), who are responsible for coordinating safeguarding across the school. They ensure that concerns are handled swiftly, sensitively, and in line with statutory procedures.

pageCache.text:
Join us at one of our Open Days to discover the incredible opportunities on offer for your son at Arnold House
Discover Arnold House In Person
Our Open Mornings typically last for about two hours and will take you on the journey from 3+ to 13+ across our Pre-Prep and Prep schools. We begin at our Pre-Prep, where tours will be led by the Head of Pre-Prep and the Registrar. During this time, you will be able to see our boys from Pre-Reception to Year 1 on a typical school day, where you may find them climbing in the playground, singing in their music lesson or talking excitedly about their most recent inquiry led topic.
Hear From Our Senior Boys
Following the tour of the Pre-Prep, you will take a short walk up to our Prep School where tours of the facilities are led by our Year 8 boys. We feel very passionately about creating opportunities for parents to meet our most senior boys and hear first-hand about their own school experiences. There will also be an opportunity to meet some current parents, which provides a useful insight into their experiences as Arnold House parents.
The morning will finish with a talk from the Headmaster and an opportunity to stay and ask any questions you might have at the end.
